title: Keep private product data local and use scoped model connections for ordinary work
context: ScopeHub serves individual users beyond its co-developers. A real model is needed for financial collaboration while personal conversations, memory and strategies remain under each user’s local control.
decision: Use the local profile as the authority for private content and derived records. Activating a model grants the ordinary conversation and workspace scope disclosed by that route. Attach saved private content only from an exact user-selected preview for that request and recipient. Qualify cloud and local capabilities with actual behavior. Develop in Herdr using task-scoped roles and independent verification.
authority: The owner selected previewed excerpts, authorized ordinary use upon connecting a model and delegated implementation tooling and parallelism. See contracts/reviews/2026-11-19-development-and-local-data.json.

alternatives.option: Ask for authorization on every routine model turn.
alternatives.reason: It interrupts already authorized work without changing the data or destination.

alternatives.option: Automatically attach persistent user memory after activating a cloud connection.
alternatives.reason: The owner authorized only selected private excerpts for the current request.

consequences: The Rust core owns local persistence, user scope and the final outbound projection. A changed model destination or excerpt is a new disclosure. A restored backup cannot replay an old attachment grant.
Use development permissions for project tooling and synthetic verification. Every product user independently controls their own model connection, records and externally visible operations.
The product task ledger owns implementation of persistence and actual model-client dispatch. Passing a fixture scores the verification mechanism; a configured session needs real qualification.
revisit_when: A new persistent content type, data recipient or synchronization service changes local-profile or disclosure semantics.
Actual provider capability, user experience or the observed cost of distributed development changes the chosen workflow.
